title: Unified Surface: Minimum Viable Behavioral Spec & Launch Rundown for Hosted Generation Endpoints
creator: Asha Patel
summary: Define the minimum viable behavioral specification (inputs, outputs, errors, edge-cases) and a practical launch rundown for the hosted generation surface (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Clarify ambiguous requirements discovered during API harmonization and freeze acceptance criteria for GA rollout.
background: Over the last two quarters we've been consolidating multiple generation endpoints into a consistent hosted surface. Workstreams have converged on a single API shape but teams continue to surface differences (streaming semantics, structured output guarantees, rerank input shapes, embedding normalization). This ticket collects the behavioral spec that the platform will guarantee at launch and lists the engineering and operational steps required to validate and ship the initial GA bundle.
goals: Produce a tightly-scoped PRD that removes ambiguity for SDKs and SDK parity tests
Lock acceptance criteria for each endpoint (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank)
Document required runtime behaviors and fallbacks for GA hosted surface
Create an actionable launch checklist for eng/ops/pm to run before releasing the surface
non_goals: Designing post-GA features (tools/function-calling expansion, multimodal inputs beyond existing roadmap)
Large API surface rework that requires breaking changes to existing customers
On-prem package changes — Private/Dedicated parity will be tracked in separate tickets
scope_changes: Initial plan included a strict typed schema for structured outputs; we will instead ship with recommended JSON-schema examples and 'best-effort' validation to unblock GA
Dropped automatic per-customer rerank weighting tuning for GA due to time constraints; will be tracked as an Optimize workstream
Expanded acceptance criteria to include network-ready regional fallback behavior after experiments showed cross-region flakiness
requirements: Chat endpoint must support streaming chunked UTF-8 tokens with idempotent resume tokens for 1 minute of disconnect
Completions endpoint must preserve prompt metadata (user_id, request_id) in traces and logs for debugability
Embeddings must be L2-normalized by default and expose a parameter `normalize=false` for customers that require raw vectors
Rerank must accept arrays of up to 128 candidates, return deterministic scores for identical inputs, and preserve original candidate order in ties
All endpoints must return consistent error codes and structured error objects (code, message, retriable boolean, details array)
api_contracts: Chat: POST /v1/chat - supports messages array, system/user/assistant role convention, streaming via SSE and chunked JSON lines
Completions: POST /v1/completions - accepts prompt string | array, stop sequences list, max_tokens, temperature, top_p
Embeddings: POST /v1/embeddings - batch inputs of up to 512 items (size quota enforced), default embedding dimension 1536, response includes vector and metadata
Rerank: POST /v1/rerank - accepts { query, candidates: [{id, text, metadata}] }, returns scores array aligned to candidates
behavioral_guarantees: Backward compatibility: existing 'legacy_chat' endpoint will be maintained for 90 days with traffic migration tooling
Streaming safety: either full-token or partial-token chunk boundaries will never violate UTF-8 sequences
Determinism window: for fixed model+temperature=0 and identical inputs, completions and rerank will be deterministic across replicas
Privacy: user-provided metadata will not be used to train public models; audit log entries identify retention TTL
performance_slos: Completions: p95 token latency <= 200ms (local dev baseline: 120ms)
Chat streaming: first-byte latency p95 <= 300ms, steady-state throughput >= 300 tokens/s per allocated GPU pool
Embeddings: p95 per-request latency for batch size 1 <= 120ms, batch-optimized throughput target 10k embeddings/min/per-pool
acceptance_criteria: API contract matches the documented schema and SDK tests pass (JS/Python)
Integration tests against staging verify streaming resume behavior and deterministic rerank scoring
End-to-end load tests demonstrate that the hosted capacity template sustains 80% of expected initial GA traffic with headroom for autoscaling
Security review completed and KMS integration validated for metadata at-rest encryption
Observability: per-request token/cost telemetry available, per-model latency and error dashboards created
Migration: sample migration playbook for customers on legacy endpoints validated with 3 pilot customers
launch_checklist: Finalize PRD and publish as canonical Confluence page
Create SDK compatibility test matrix and add gating CI job
Add feature flags for staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback thresholds
Provision dedicated canary capacity in two regions and run 72-hour soak
Run red-team test for structured output to ensure schema compatibility and safety filters
Run chaos tests for network partition and verify streaming resume behavior
Confirm incident runbook and oncall rotation for first 4 weeks post-GA
Announce breaking-change windows and deprecation timeline to affected customers
Coordinate marketplace and billing hooks for token-based usage recording
Final signoff from Security, Reliability, and Developer Experience leads
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal beta behind feature flag for 2 weeks (internal apps + SDK smoke tests)
Phase 1: External beta with invited customers (10% traffic) for 3 weeks, collect quality metrics and customer feedback
Phase 2: Gradual expansion to 50% with automated anomaly detection monitoring costs and error rates
Phase 3: Full GA after 2 weeks at 50% with clean metrics and no critical regressions
monitoring_and_sla: SLO: 99.9% success rate for requests with non-5xx responses in each region
Alert: p95 latency breach for any endpoint triggers P1 page
Cost guardrail: per-customer token burn rate anomaly detection to trigger throttles and billing alerts
Quality tracking: prompt set evaluations run nightly; regression >2% triggers rollback window
qa_plan: Unit and integration tests in CI for all contract shapes
End-to-end smoke tests using recorded golden prompts and expected output signatures
Performance harness runs with representative traffic profile and verified baselines
Manual exploratory QA on streaming for edge-case encodings and long prompts
notes: We intentionally allow `normalize=false` for embeddings to satisfy early enterprise users with custom downstream pipelines
Determinism guarantee limited to model+seed+temperature=0; random seeds introduced by sampling parameters will not be deterministic
We will publish a migration guide and a client-side shim for legacy consumers to ease adoption
